pr.title: coverage: Make counter creation handle node/edge counters more uniformly
pr.description:
Similar to #130380, this is another round of small improvements informed by my ongoing attempts to overhaul coverage counter creation.

One of the big benefits is getting rid of the awkward special-case that would sometimes attach an edge counter to a node instead. That was needed by the code that chooses which out-edge should be given a counter expression, but we can avoid that by making the corresponding check a little smarter.

I've also renamed several things to be simpler and more consistent, which should help with future changes.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: The supplied PR and frozen analysis establish only a counter-representation/placement refactor in InstrumentCoverage, not a semantic miscompile. The removed special case attached an out-edge expression to the target node when the target had a sole predecessor; the replacement stores the same expression in edge_counters, and the new make_node_counter_inner later reuses that sole-in-edge counter for the target node. The candidate filter is adjusted correspondingly (edge already has a counter, or its sole predecessor is the source and the target node already has a counter), so the effective counter value associated with every node/edge is preserved. Any source-grounded pair modeling this rewrite would keep node and edge execution-count values identical; producing differing original/transformed outputs would require adding an unrelated bug (e.g., dropping the sole-in-edge reuse, reregistering a counter, or changing the expression formula), which would not be the historical transformation. Therefore no valid Miri-checkable counterexample exists from this PR material.

analysis.originalLogic:
Coverage counter construction traverses the `CoverageGraph`, assigns a node counter to each BCB that needs one, and (for out-summable nodes) may choose one out-edge to receive an expression equal to the source node counter minus the sum of the other out-edge counters. The old implementation detected whether an out-edge already had a counter through `edge_has_no_counter`: if the target had a sole predecessor, it inspected `bcb_counters[to_bcb]`, otherwise it inspected `bcb_edge_counters`. After creating the chosen expression, if the target had a sole predecessor, the old code attached the expression to the target node: "This edge normally wouldn't get its own counter, so attach the expression to its target node instead, so that `edge_has_no_counter` can see it."

The PR makes node and edge counters uniform: node counters are memoized in `node_counters`, edge counters in `edge_counters`, and `make_node_counter_inner`/`make_edge_counter_inner` reuse equivalent counters. A node whose sole in-edge already has a counter reuses that edge counter; an edge whose target has a sole predecessor reuses the target node counter; an edge whose source has a simple successor reuses the source node counter. The out-edge candidate filter now ignores edges that already have counters, or "could use the existing counter of their target node", and the chosen expression is always stored with `set_edge_counter(from_bcb, target_bcb, expression)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, an expression for the chosen out-edge was sometimes not stored as an edge counter at all: when the target BCB had exactly one predecessor, the code called `set_bcb_counter(expression_to_bcb, expression)` and therefore attached the edge's expression to the target node. This special case is the transformation removed by the PR. It was not demonstrated by the supplied material to produce wrong execution counts; the PR describes it as "the awkward special-case that would sometimes attach an edge counter to a node instead" and says the special-case can be avoided by making the candidate check "a little smarter". The replacement attaches the expression to the edge unconditionally, while the candidate filter accounts for a target node counter only when the target's sole predecessor is the source. A separate agent should therefore treat this as a counter-representation/placement transformation, not as evidence of a confirmed miscompile.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented MIR control-flow graphs (`CoverageGraph`) where BCBs need coverage counters: branch nodes whose out-edges are summable, targets with zero/one/multiple predecessors, sources with a simple successor, loops and reloop/exit out-edges, and nodes whose count can be derived from the sole incoming edge counter. The relevant distinctions are graph-shape predicates (`sole_predecessor`, `simple_successor`, `is_out_summable`) and whether a node/edge counter already exists, not the source language feature that produced the CFG.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage counter creation previously attached an out-edge expression to the target node when that target had a sole predecessor, and used a special `edge_has_no_counter` check to notice it. The PR stores every out-edge expression in `edge_counters`, memoizes node/edge counters, reuses equivalent sole-in-edge/simple-successor counters, and makes the out-edge candidate check skip edges that already have counters or whose sole-predecessor target already has a node counter. This is a uniformity/refactor optimization of counter placement, not a demonstrated coverage-count bug fix.
analysis.trigger: When constructing counters for a CoverageGraph, especially when a source BCB is out-summable and one of its out-edges leads to a target BCB whose sole predecessor is that source; also when a node's sole in-edge already has a counter or an edge's source has a simple successor.
preconditions: A CoverageGraph with BCBs marked in `bcb_needs_counter`.
Counter creation is traversing nodes in loop-aware order via `TraverseCoverageGraphWithLoops`.
The source node is `is_out_summable`, otherwise no edge candidates are considered.
An edge may already have a counter, or its target may have a sole predecessor and an existing node counter.
Node and edge counters must each be set at most once, so outer get-or-make wrappers perform memoization before the inner creation paths call setters.
pitfalls: Do not attach an edge expression to a node merely because the target has a sole predecessor; store it in the edge counter map so node and edge counter identities remain separate.

The candidate filter must skip both edges that already have edge counters and edges that can use the target node's existing counter; checking only the old sole-predecessor node slot misses the new uniform representation.

Memoization must occur in `get_or_make_node_counter` and `get_or_make_edge_counter`; `set_node_counter`/`set_edge_counter` assert that no existing counter is replaced, so repeated creation without the wrapper would panic rather than silently overwrite.
Reusing a target node counter for a sole-predecessor edge or a source node counter for a simple-successor edge is valid only when the graph predicates guarantee equal execution counts.
When building an edge expression, compute the sum of all other out-edge counters while excluding the chosen target, then subtract that sum from the source node counter.
Do not infer a semantic miscompile or coverage-count discrepancy from the removed node-attachment special case; the supplied patch contains no regression-test change or execution evidence.
analysis.testStrategy: Use coverage UI tests that dump coverage counters/expressions (or coverage MIR) on CFGs covering: a branch whose chosen out-edge target has a sole predecessor, including the case where that target already has a node counter; a branch target with multiple predecessors; a source with a simple successor; loop/reloop edges; and a node whose sole in-edge already has a counter. Assert the expected counter/expression placement and that no node or edge is assigned two counters. Compare coverage counter graphs across programs that differ only in whether the sole-predecessor target already has a node counter, keeping the CFG shape otherwise identical. The supplied patch itself contains no regression test changes, so tests must be designed rather than cited.
